data.purpose: User-directed assurance for 10M+ LOC systems: end-to-end specification compliance, upward mandatory safety and strong provenance, pointwise proofs, program-author obligations first and Grass implementation complexity second. Audit cross-stack factoring and legacy source/binary safety. No product implementation, coordination, or agent-bus/tooling audit.

data.expected: Close Hello World through exact source/raw instructions/encoding/artifact/selected target semantics; independently mutate a byte, instruction and relocation and reject stale certificates.
data.observed_behavior: MachineCertificate has no exact source/encoding index. ArtifactFormat supplies its own loadedBehavior; the fixture certifies empty bytes with a constant model. This is an acknowledged foundation limit, not a false theorem. Related to g-foundation:94; this request specifically tracks exact source-to-target artifact correspondence, not a second mandatory-demand ruling.

data.summary: [A1] Production emission must bind exact assembly to selected target semantics

data.expected: Show distinct instruction sequences reusing one portable proof through segment/weak simulation or a proved summary; account for intermediate safety and reject hidden infinite stuttering under a termination claim.
data.observed_behavior: Each concrete step maps to one abstract step preserving its audit event. This constrains instruction insertions and multi-instruction realizations unless a separately proved boundary semantics supplies the bridge. Expressiveness risk, not unsoundness.

data.expected: Account for the existing lookup_of_own_entry helper. Show whether general equivalent-spec lookup can also avoid caller-written unique; remove redundant interface evidence only if consumer or maintenance cost improves. Retaining it with evidence of benefit is an acceptable disposition.
data.observed_behavior: ExactStandardRealizerLookup asks for unique while lookupUniquenessIsRedundant derives it from existing inputs. Known redundancy is a concrete unnecessary witness obligation. Correction/narrowing: lookup_of_own_entry already derives this for the own-entry case. This is a low-priority library factoring concern; no claim that every application currently writes this proof manually.

data.expected: Demonstrate reusable composition for two emitting subsystems preserving required global order. Replacing graphics must not reopen unrelated storage internals solely because both emit. Measure consumer proof burden before adding wrappers.
data.observed_behavior: at_most_one_lens_may_emit shows two disjoint lenses cannot both touch the shared pending fragment. This creates a shared-boundary proof obligation for otherwise separate emitting subsystems; local composition is not proven impossible.

data.expected: Compare a representative current transition with a typed local-update construction deriving unchanged fields and scope. Preserve relational nondeterminism. Count independent caller choices, residual goals and change scope; retain only abstractions that reduce total system burden.
data.observed_behavior: Before/after transition records repeatedly require explicit scope and unchanged-field clauses. Module histories record omissions later found by preservation proofs. This is a maintenance-risk investigation, not a claim that file size proves excess or an assertion of measured historical growth. Concrete change sample: commit 830b5a2 adds identity distinctness across 4 Grass modules and 6 fixture modules; 200 lines added to WellFormedness. It already factors two useful generic lemmas, creates_nothing_distinct and created_identities_distinct. The remaining question is whether repeated per-constructor new-identity clauses can derive from a shared ledger update. Counts include comments/tests and do not alone establish excess.
reproduction: lake build passed all 181 jobs at this snapshot; Spikes remain noncompiling design fixtures.
data.summary: [C3] Assess recurring manual transition preservation obligations
